name: Virtual CRISPR Difficult Benchmark
description: 1,814 balanced gene-phenotype queries curated from two late-2024 CRISPR screen publications.

attributes.version: Manually curated from PMID 39567689 (Chen et al. 2024, gliocidin) and PMID 39385035 (Skoulidis et al. 2024, PD1 blockade)
attributes.population: 1,814 gene-phenotype queries from two knockout screens in NG2-3112 mouse glioblastoma cells and 3LL Lewis lung carcinoma cells; 907 positive and 907 negative
attributes.label_semantics: Same high-confidence hit definition as the Simple Benchmark. To balance labels, each significant effect opposite to the hypothesised phenotype was also posed as an inverted query and labelled a hit.
attributes.scope_note: Table 4 per screen (Genes, Hits): 39567689 increased sensitivity to gliocidin (881, 73); 39385035 increased resistance to PD1 blockade (26, 23); 39567689 decreased sensitivity to gliocidin (881, 808); 39385035 decreased resistance to PD1 blockade (26, 3). The 808 and 23 rows are the inverted phenotypes. Each screen appears once per phenotype direction with the same gene count, so 2 x (881 + 26) = 1,814 queries.

name: Virtual CRISPR BioGRID-ORCS training set
description: Training set for the Virtual CRISPR embedding classifier: 1,678 BioGRID-ORCS screens in human or mouse cells.

attributes.population: 1,678 screens (from 1,924) performed in human or mouse cells; about 22.6 million gene-level results across 3 perturbation methods, 40,461 genes, 133 cell lines and 613 phenotype descriptions; 7.74% of gene-phenotype pairs are hits
attributes.split: 5 randomly selected screens held out as a validation set for early stopping and hyperparameter tuning
attributes.label_semantics: High-confidence hit definition; screens reporting both significant positive and negative effects for the same gene-phenotype query were excluded. The full BioGRID-ORCS phenotype note is embedded rather than a parsed phenotype.

scope_note.note: The paper does not say whether the four Simple Benchmark screens were removed from the training set; the classifier is evaluated only on the Difficult Benchmark

version.note: Section 3 says 'From the BioGRID-ORCS database'; only the benchmark source is given as v1.1.16 (Section 2.1)

name: Virtual CRISPR Simple Benchmark
description: 1,175 gene-phenotype queries from four BioGRID-ORCS screens, each labelled hit or no-hit.

attributes.version: BioGRID-ORCS v1.1.16; screens 1837, 1885, 1835 and 1733
attributes.population: 1,175 gene-phenotype queries from four manually selected BioGRID-ORCS screens; 41.3% are hits
attributes.assay: CRISPR activation and knockout screens harmonised by BioGRID-ORCS
attributes.label_semantics: A hit is a statistically significant effect in the hypothesised direction; a no-hit is a statistically significant effect in the opposite direction. Genes with no significant effect are not queried.
attributes.scope_note: Table 3 per screen (Genes, Hits): 1837 activation, primary CD4+ human T cells, increased TNF-alpha secretion (423, 140); 1885 activation, J774 macrophages, phagocytic inhibition (343, 139); 1835 activation, primary CD4+ human T cells, increased IL2 secretion (243, 76); 1733 knockout, HeLa cervical adenocarcinoma cells, increased RelA nuclear translocation (166, 130). Genes counts are after filtering to genes with a significant effect.

positives.note: Only the 41.3% hit fraction and per-screen hit counts are printed, not a benchmark total. The Table 3 hit counts (140, 139, 76, 130) sum to 485 of 1,175, which matches 41.3%.

name: Raw Emb. on the Virtual CRISPR Difficult Benchmark
description: Published comparison; transcribed, not reproduced.

attributes.version: Primary source as retrieved 2026-10-22

comparison.dataset_version: Curated from PMID 39567689 and PMID 39385035
comparison.split: Fixed evaluation set of 1,814 queries; no data from BioGRID-ORCS
comparison.inputs: Text of the perturbation method, gene symbol, cell line and phenotype, each embedded with text-embedding-3-large (raw text, or a GPT-4o summary for Summ. Emb.) and concatenated
comparison.metric_implementation: AUROC and AUPRC from predicted probabilities; other metrics after binarising with Youden's J statistic
comparison.adaptation: Supervised MLP on LLM embeddings, trained on BioGRID-ORCS
comparison.aggregation: Single trained model; one evaluation

limitations: Authors' own method.

F1, FPR, PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity use a Youden's J threshold; the paper does not say whether it was chosen on the validation screens or on the test queries. If on the test queries these values are optimistic. AUROC and AUPRC do not depend on the threshold.
Trained on BioGRID-ORCS author hit calls; scoring it on other ORCS-derived benchmarks (for example AssayBench) would need a screen-level overlap check against its training screens.

F1, FPR, PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity use a Youden's J threshold; the paper does not say whether it was chosen on the validation screens or on the test queries. If on the test queries these values are optimistic. AUROC and AUPRC do not depend on the threshold.

name: Virtual CRISPR Difficult Benchmark: hit prediction for complex phenotypes
description: A system predicts whether a CRISPR knockout of a gene produces a complex phenotype, on balanced queries curated from two late-2024 screen publications.

attributes.protocol: Same query form as the Simple Benchmark. The embedding classifier outputs a probability, binarised with Youden's J statistic, and is scored with AUROC, AUPRC, F1, FPR, PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity. GPT-4o is scored from its binary answers, averaged across prompting strategies; AUROC and AUPRC are undefined for it.
attributes.task: Binary hit/no-hit prediction for gene-phenotype queries from CRISPR screens
attributes.version: Song et al., BioNLP 2025, Sections 2.3, 3 and 4.2
attributes.metric_definition: As for the Simple Benchmark; AUROC and AUPRC are computed from the classifier's predicted probabilities.
limitations: Binary classification of pre-selected gene-phenotype queries; there is no candidate pool, ranking step or test budget, so it measures hit prediction rather than which perturbations to test.
Only genes with a statistically significant effect in either direction are queried; genes with no effect, which make up most of a screen, are not negatives.
Retrospective: labels come from published screens and no new experiment was run.
Labels are balanced by construction: every gene appears once per phenotype direction with opposite labels, so the benchmark tests whether the direction of effect is predicted.
Two screens from two publications, both in mouse cells; the authors call the test set constrained by the availability of suitable post-cutoff screens.
No random-baseline row is printed for this benchmark.

The Youden's J threshold is chosen on predicted probabilities; the paper does not say whether it was set on the validation set or on the test set. Threshold-dependent metrics (F1, FPR, PPV, NPV, sensitivity, specificity) may be optimistic for the embedding classifier; AUROC and AUPRC are not affected.
attributes.source_locator: Sections 2.3, 3 and 4.2; Table 2; Appendix A.3 and Table 4; Limitations

name: Virtual CRISPR Simple Benchmark: yes/no prediction of a screen hit
description: A system answers whether a stated CRISPR perturbation of a gene in a cell line causally produces a stated phenotype, scored against high-confidence hit labels from four BioGRID-ORCS screens.

attributes.protocol: Each query is posed as 'Does {perturbation method} of {gene} in {cell line} causally result in {phenotype}?' and the system answers Yes (hit) or No (no-hit). Prompted language models are run with zero-shot, one- or two-shot and chain-of-thought prompts at temperature 0 with a fixed seed; the binary answer is extracted from the generated text. Metrics: F1 and false positive rate, with PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity for GPT-4o and the random baseline in Appendix Table 8.
attributes.task: Binary hit/no-hit prediction for gene-phenotype queries from CRISPR screens
attributes.version: Song et al., BioNLP 2025, Sections 2.2, 2.3, 4.1 and Appendix A.1-A.2
attributes.metric_definition: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall for the hit class; FPR is the proportion of actual negatives predicted positive. Under the high-confidence definition a false positive asserts an effect opposite to the observed significant effect.
attributes.control: Random baseline predicting hit with probability equal to the benchmark's overall hit proportion (Appendix A.2)
limitations: Binary classification of pre-selected gene-phenotype queries; there is no candidate pool, ranking step or test budget, so it measures hit prediction rather than which perturbations to test.
Only genes with a statistically significant effect in either direction are queried; genes with no effect, which make up most of a screen, are not negatives.
Retrospective: labels come from published screens and no new experiment was run.
The four screens were selected by the authors from BioGRID-ORCS on domain knowledge, and are public, so prompted models may have seen them or their source papers in pre-training.
Table 1 values are means across up to 10 prompting-strategy combinations; the o1 family was run without explicit chain-of-thought prompts, so its n is smaller and not printed.

name: Retrospective active learning on a fully measured two-gene CRISPR viability screen: top-200 gene pairs found by round 4
description: Starting from a uniformly sampled seed set shared by all acquisition functions, a model ensemble is retrained each round on the measured pairs acquired so far and an acquisition function picks the next batch; the score counts how many of the screen's 200 strongest measured pairs are among the 200 strongest of the measured-plus-predicted values.

attributes.protocol: Round 0 trains on a uniformly sampled seed set (100 pairs for Norman, 500 for Simpson and both Horlbeck screens). In each of 4 further rounds the trained ensemble predicts every unmeasured pair, the acquisition function selects 100 (Norman) or 500 (others) more pairs whose measured values are revealed from the screen, and the model is retrained. Acquisition functions: Uniform, Maximum Predicted Effect (MPE), Upper Confidence Bound (UCB, residual from a linear model plus ensemble standard deviation, kappa = 1), Uncertainty (ensemble standard deviation) and Mean-UCB (alpha times ensemble mean plus beta times ensemble standard deviation).
attributes.procedure: Fraction Discovered (Appendix D): after training in round i, predictions for all unseen pairs are concatenated with the measured values of the seen pairs to form X_i; X_i,P is the top P values of X_i, Y_i,P the top P measured values across all samples, and P_i = |X_i,P ∩ Y_i,P|. Tables 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 print P_i at P = 200; Table 3 prints the marginal gain (P_4 - P_0)/4.
attributes.version: Qin et al. 2025, PMLR 267, Sections 4.3 and 5.3, Appendices C and D
attributes.unit_detail: gene pairs, out of the 200 strongest measured pairs
attributes.metric_definition: P_200 = number of the 200 strongest measured gene pairs in the whole screen that are among the 200 strongest values of the combined set of measured (acquired) and predicted (unacquired) pairs. Pairs counted as found need not have been measured.
attributes.task: Choose which two-gene combinations to measure next so that the strongest combinations are identified with few measurements
attributes.selection: Candidate pool is every pair in the screen; the seed set is drawn uniformly and shared by all acquisition functions
attributes.replicates: Tables 4, 5, 7 and 8: three cross-fold replicates with standard error printed. Tables 2 and 3: not stated.
attributes.scope_note: Retrospective replay over already-measured screens; no new experiment is run. 'Strongest' is not defined by sign: Appendix C.2 says MPE selects the highest absolute predicted effects, and Appendix D says top P values.
limitations: A pair counts as discovered when it is in the top 200 of the measured-plus-predicted ranking, so the count mixes pairs actually measured with pairs only predicted; it is not the number of strong pairs among those tested.

Ground truth is the 200 strongest measured viability effects in the same screen, not an independently confirmed phenotype or a significance threshold; the 200 are 3.2% of Norman's 6,328 pairs and 0.14% to 0.21% of the other screens.
The measurement budget differs by screen (500 pairs of 6,328 for Norman; 2,500 of 95,703 to 147,658 for the others).
Single-gene effects of every gene are available to the model throughout.
All values come from the NAIAD authors, who also adapted RECOVER and GEARS to this setting.
The paper does not define a cross-fold replicate for the active-learning experiments.

name: Combination phenotype prediction from small training sets: test RMSE at fixed average gene frequency

limitations: Tables 2 and 3 print no uncertainty and do not say how many replicates they summarise. Their values differ from Table 4 for the same model and acquisition function by more than rounding (MPE on Horlbeck Jurkat: 161 in Table 2, 150.0 (4.0) in Table 4).
Table 7 and Table 4 agree for NAIAD MPE and RECOVER MPE on Norman at round 4 but differ for NAIAD Uniform (93.7 (0.7) in Table 7, 93.3 (0.7) in Table 4).

The ensemble size behind Tables 2 to 4, 7 and 8 is not stated; no row of Table 5 equals the Table 4 values.
Figures 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 print no values; the drug-combination results (Section 5.4, Figure 5) are not extracted.

Appendix C.5 equates Mean-UCB with beta = 0 to MPE, but Table 8 at beta = 0 differs from Table 4 NAIAD MPE (Norman 138.3 (2.2) against 143.0 (1.5); Simpson 145.7 (3.8) against 141.7 (3.7)), so the two tables are separate runs.
Table 7 prints NAIAD's round-0 count on Norman as 86.0 (1.0); Tables 2 and 3 imply 88 for the same seed set, consistent with Table 2 being a separate run.
Table 8's caption calls the printed values a true positive rate (TPR), but they are counts out of 200, like Tables 2, 4, 5 and 7.

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix A.2 describes the random baseline as predicting hit with probability equal to 'the overall proportion of actual hits in the specific benchmark dataset'. With one pooled rate (485 of 1,175 = 41.3%, Table 3) the expected PPV, sensitivity, F1 and FPR are all about 0.41 and specificity and NPV about 0.59. Table 8 prints PPV 0.47, sensitivity 0.46, F1 0.47, FPR 0.36, specificity 0.64 and NPV 0.63. With each screen's own hit rate (Table 3) the expected values are 0.47, 0.47, 0.47, 0.37, 0.63 and 0.63, which match. One draw at the pooled rate would need sensitivity about 2 standard errors above and FPR about 3 below expectation at once. The baseline therefore probably uses per-screen hit rates, which is information a screen designer would not have before the screen. The expected values were computed by the reviewer from Table 3 counts and are not stored as results. Treat the random row as a per-screen-prevalence classifier, not a matched random-selection comparator.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix A.2; Table 3; Table 1, row "Random Baseline"; Table 8, row "Random N/A N/A"

name: AssayBench-Loop test split (20 genome-wide CRISPR screens published after 2021)
description: The 20 temporally held-out test screens of AssayBench-Loop, each a genome-wide CRISPR screen with binary hit labels.

attributes.version: AssayBench-Loop as described in arXiv:2609.11877v1
attributes.split: Temporal: 1,349 training screens before 2021, 20 validation screens from 2021, 20 test screens after 2021
attributes.subset_scope: Test screens were restricted to genome-wide coverage (18,000-22,000 genes), at least 50 hits with hit rate below 15%, and a best-LLM AnDCG@100 of at least 0.05 (Gemini 3.1 Pro on AssayBench); phenotype categories were allocated from the eligible pool with a soft cap of six per category, and within-category diversity of screen descriptions was maximised.
attributes.source_dataset: AssayBench (1,920 CRISPR screens); the test pool is AssayBench's post-2021 split
limitations: Screens were selected, not sampled: the criteria include a performance floor for the best LLM on AssayBench, which conditions the test set on LLM-recoverable hits.
Hit labels are each screen's own published significance call; the candidate pool G (about 20,000 genes) is larger than each screen library, so genes outside the library cannot be scored.

Not linked same_data_as to tgtval-20261009-data-assaybench-test: the 20 screens are a selected subset of AssayBench's post-2021 test pool (Methods 4.2), not the same data, and their identities (Supplementary Table 2) were not matched to AssayBench entries.
attributes.source_locator: Section 2.1; Figure 2B-C caption; Methods 4.2; Supplementary Table 2 (not extracted)

name: AssayBench-Loop adaptive hit discovery: 10 rounds of 100 genes on 20 held-out CRISPR screens
description: Retrospective replay in which a policy picks 100 genes per round for 10 rounds from a shared pool of about 20,000 genes, sees each screen's historical hit labels for its picks, and is scored on hits found against random selection.

attributes.protocol: For each test screen the policy receives a natural-language description of the screen. At each of T = 10 rounds it nominates b = 100 genes from the candidate pool G, observes their binary hit labels from the historical screen, and conditions the next batch on the accumulated history. Budget 1,000 acquisitions per screen (about 5% of the library). Methods may use the 1,349 training screens. Metrics are computed per screen and averaged equally over the 20 test screens.
attributes.version: arXiv:2609.11877v1, Section 2.1, Methods 4.1-4.3, Appendix H; Table 1 and Supplementary Table 4
attributes.metric_definition: EF = |G_T ∩ H| / ((N_L + N_Ḡ + N_miss) · h_rand), where G_T is the set of acquired genes, H the screen's hits, N_L the acquired genes in the screen library, N_Ḡ the hallucinated (invalid) gene names, N_miss the unfilled slots and h_rand = |H|/|L| the screen's hit rate. Valid genes outside the screen library are not counted in the denominator. Secondary: nAUC, fraction of hits found, shortfall, %ess, Vendi ratio, pathway overlap, EP-B/EP-S/EP-D (Appendix H).
attributes.aggregation: Each metric computed per screen, then averaged with equal weight over the 20 test screens (EP-D is computed over the pooled test set).
attributes.allowed_information: Screen description (cell line, perturbation modality, treatment, readout, hit definition); the genes acquired in earlier rounds and their hit labels; the 1,349 training screens. Policies may ignore any of these (the label-ablation arms omit the hit labels).
heldout_validation: 20 screens from 2021; used to select the handoff round k = 3
attributes.selection: Test screens filtered for genome-wide coverage, at least 50 hits, hit rate below 15%, and a best-LLM AnDCG@100 of at least 0.05, then chosen for phenotype spread and description diversity.

uncertainty_reporting.printed: Table 1 and Supplementary Table 4 print means without spread.
uncertainty_reporting.runs: Not stated, except that Random is one draw.
uncertainty_reporting.note: Supplementary Figure 6D shows ±1 SEM across 20 screens for five methods as a figure only.

limitations: Retrospective: labels are historical screen calls, and the authors state the policies remain to be validated prospectively in a live experimental loop.
The held-out unit is the screen; there are 20 test screens and no per-screen values in the extracted tables.
Test screens were selected with a performance floor for the best LLM on AssayBench, which favours screens whose hits an LLM can name.
Recovered hits are often DepMap common-essential genes (the %ess column), so a high EF can partly reflect generic fitness genes.
Random is one draw of the random policy, not its expectation (Table 1 caption).
The AssayLoop, AssayFormer and AssayLLM rows are the authors' own methods; all other rows were also run by the same authors.

name: Biology-in-the-loop: Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens
description: Preprint introducing the AssayBench-Loop benchmark of 1,389 historical CRISPR screens and the AssayLoop, AssayFormer and AssayLLM acquisition policies.

attributes.version: arXiv:2609.11877 version 1, submitted 2026-09-10; not peer reviewed
attributes.source_locator: Full artifact bytes; per-record locators on each record
attributes.access_and_reuse: CC-BY-4.0 permits redistribution of the article bytes.
attributes.archive_note: Not archived in the batch; the artifact_sha256 pins the bytes read. The digest matches the copy hashed for the 2026-10-07 dossier and the 2026-10-22 search pass.
attributes.scope_note: Authors are at Genentech. Two of them (De Brouwer, Scalia) are also authors of AssayBench (tgtval-20261009-source-debrouwer2026), on which AssayBench-Loop is built.

name: Relevance of AssayBench-Loop adaptive hit discovery: 10 rounds of 100 genes on 20 held-out CRISPR screens to "Select perturbations for a defined cellular response"
description: The closest stored evidence to the use case's comparison question: every policy picks from the same gene pool for the same screens at the same 1,000-gene budget and is scored on hits found against a random policy on those screens. Proxy, because the screens are replayed with historical labels, a hit is each screen's own significance call, and the test screens were chosen with a performance floor for the best language model.

attributes.endpoint: Hit enrichment factor over the random expectation, fraction of each screen's hits found, normalised cumulative-hit AUC, shortfall and share of common-essential hits after 10 rounds of 100 genes, mean over 20 genome-wide CRISPR screens published after 2021, for 53 configurations: one random draw, a prior-hit baseline, Screen-kNN, random forests, third-party adaptive design methods (BPMF, MAML, BioBO, Probability-of-Hit, Transformer + DAgger), language models used directly with and without hit labels, agent harnesses, and the authors' AssayFormer, AssayLLM and AssayLoop handoffs
attributes.rationale: The closest stored evidence to the use case's comparison question: every policy picks from the same gene pool for the same screens at the same 1,000-gene budget and is scored on hits found against a random policy on those screens. Proxy, because the screens are replayed with historical labels, a hit is each screen's own significance call, and the test screens were chosen with a performance floor for the best language model. Every row, including the third-party methods, the language models and the random draw, was run by the authors of AssayFormer and AssayLoop with their own prompts and history format. It covers single genes in screens whose phenotype is set by each source study, not a response the user prespecifies, and no combinations.
constraints: Compare configurations only within this protocol; do not pool with the CPPC, NAIAD or AssayBench protocols. The test screens are drawn from AssayBench, so agreement with the AssayBench evaluations is not independent.

Random is one draw of the random policy, not its expectation. EF is defined against the random expectation, so a random policy scores about 1 by construction; fraction of hits found and nAUC are the columns where the random row adds information.
The rows without hit labels are the authors' label ablation under the same protocol inputs; read them against their labelled arm, not as a separate benchmark.
EP-B, EP-S, EP-D, Vendi and pathway-overlap values are breadth diagnostics, not hit yield, and the three EP scopes are not comparable with each other.
Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and limitations before citing a result.
limitations: Retrospective: labels are historical screen calls, and the authors state the policies remain to be validated prospectively in a live experimental loop.
20 test screens and means only: Table 1 and Supplementary Table 4 print no uncertainty, and the number of runs per row is unreported.

Test screens were filtered for genome-wide coverage, at least 50 hits, hit rate below 15% and a best-LLM AnDCG@100 of at least 0.05, which favours screens whose hits a language model can name; the authors say the benchmark is not an unbiased sample of genome-wide CRISPR screens.
The temporal split is relative to the 1,349 training screens; the paper does not say whether the test screens or their publications predate the language models' training data.

Many recovered hits are DepMap common-essential genes (18.6% for the random draw, 99.1% for the prior-hit baseline), so part of any enrichment can reflect generic fitness genes rather than the screen's specific phenotype.
Author-run: AssayFormer, AssayLLM and AssayLoop are the authors' methods, and the authors also ran every comparator; third-party rows are the authors' runs, not those methods' own published results.
The random policy's sampling universe (the shared gene pool or each screen's library) is not stated.
Preprint (arXiv v1), not peer reviewed.

name: Relevance of Retrospective active learning on a fully measured two-gene CRISPR viability screen: top-200 gene pairs found by round 4 to "Select perturbations for a defined cellular response"
description: The only stored evidence on choosing which gene combinations to test: acquisition strategies compared at a fixed number of measured pairs from a shared seed set. Proxy, because the count includes strong pairs the model only predicted, the truth is the 200 largest viability effects in the same screen, and the screens are replayed rather than tested.

attributes.endpoint: Number of each screen's 200 strongest measured gene pairs that fall in the top 200 of the measured-plus-predicted ranking after four rounds of active learning (and by round, ensemble size and UCB weight), on four fully measured two-gene CRISPR viability screens (Norman, Simpson, Horlbeck K562, Horlbeck Jurkat), for NAIAD, RECOVER and GEARS under uniform, maximum-predicted-effect, UCB, uncertainty and mean-UCB acquisition
attributes.rationale: The only stored evidence on choosing which gene combinations to test: acquisition strategies compared at a fixed number of measured pairs from a shared seed set. Proxy, because the count includes strong pairs the model only predicted, the truth is the 200 largest viability effects in the same screen, and the screens are replayed rather than tested. The use case's setting says combinations need their own protocol, and this is one. The uniform arm is NAIAD (or RECOVER) trained on randomly chosen pairs and still ranks every pair with the model, so it is a random-acquisition control, not the yield of testing randomly chosen pairs that the collection plan's random baseline would give.
constraints: Cite Table 4 (three replicates with standard error) for round-4 comparisons. Table 2 and Table 3 are separate runs with no stated run count and differ from Table 4 by more than rounding.
Compare only within one screen; the budget and the share of pairs in the top 200 differ by screen.
Do not compare this count with AssayBench-Loop's fraction of hits found or with any count of tested hits.
Do not treat the Uniform rows as the use case's random-selection baseline.
Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and limitations before citing a result.
limitations: Retrospective replay over already-measured screens; no new experiment.
A pair counts as found when it is in the top 200 of the measured-plus-predicted ranking, whether or not it was measured.

Viability phenotype only, with no significance threshold. Appendix D ranks the 'top P values' without saying whether by sign or magnitude, while MPE acquires the pairs with the highest absolute predicted effect (Appendix C).
Budgets differ: 500 measured pairs of 6,328 for Norman, 2,500 of 95,703 to 147,658 for the other screens.
The model is given every gene's single-gene effect, so combinations involving a gene with an unmeasured single effect are not covered.
Author-reported: NAIAD is the authors' method, and they adapted and ran RECOVER (from drugs to genes) and GEARS (on synthetic expression input).
At most three cross-fold replicates, which the paper does not define for active learning; Table 7 and Table 4 disagree by 0.4 on one Norman cell.
